tl;dr: How do I let a photographer know that I want to use his photos without the watermark?

I had some really, really amazing photos taken recently. I was given 3 sets of them. 2 with the photographer's business on every image to use for Instagram and other social media sites respectively, 1 of gorgeous, amazing images that are just the images, meant for print.

I want to add them to my portfolio and my social media ... but the photographer's watermark is taking away from every image. Every single one. Now, normally I don't mind watermarks. But -

It's text on a rectangular white background, and it isn't at all transparent. Exactly like Sauron in this image.The reason is because the photographer would find his work on social media with the watermark cropped or Photoshopped out entirely, so he made it extremely difficult to be removed.

I understand and wholly respect that he wants to be properly credited. I credit photographers, MUAHs, stylists, designers, and even moral support in everything I post. But the "prints" look so much better than the ones he wants me to share on social media: the watermark is plastered right in the middle of one of my favorite images. Photographers and casting directors will be looking at what I put up, and I genuinely believe the watermark will affect how they view the photos.

Without the watermark, they look like art. With it, they look unprofessional.

What do I do? I don't want to sound picky or ungrateful, but these are otherwise unquestionably the best photos I've ever received from a shoot :|
